translationRepairs: On the wushen day Lu Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Prince of Pingyuan, came to court from Tangquan; Yi Hun killed him as well.
On the wushen day Lu Li, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Masses, and Prince of Pingyuan, came to court from Tangquan; Yi Hun killed him as well.
Chinese 司徒 is Minister of the Masses; Minister of Works is 司空. The idiomatic English reverses the office.
Day wushen: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li entered court from Tangquan; Hun killed him as well.
Day wushen: Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Masses, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li entered court from Tangquan; Hun killed him as well.
Chinese 司徒 is Minister of the Masses; the literal English incorrectly uses Minister of Works.
On the dingsi day Li Bai, Duke of Fenyang, was advanced in rank to Prince of Liang.
On the dingsi day Li Bai, Duke of Pingyi, was advanced in rank to Prince of Liang.
Chinese 馮翊公 is Duke of Pingyi (Fengyi); Fenyang would be 汾陽.

Yuan Shi, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Grand General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Xihe, was to command the military affairs of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yong provinces, with Zhang Qiongqi, palace attendant giving and Marquis of Jingzhao, as deputy, to march by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.

Yuan Shi, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Grand General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Xihe, was to command the military affairs of Jing, Yu, and Southern Yong provinces, with Zhang Qiongqi, Palace Attendant and Marquis of Jingzhao, as deputy, to march by the western route to relieve Xuanhu.
English "palace attendant giving" for 給事中 is unnatural and obscures the office title.
On the bingchen day the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
On the bingshen day the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
Chinese 丙申 is the sexagenary day bingshen, not bingchen (丙辰).
Day bingchen: the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
Day bingshen: the imperial son was given the name Hong; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
Chinese 丙申 is bingshen; bingchen would be 丙辰.

On the wushen day Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain and greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin fled by night with several hundred horsemen of his retinue; his younger cousin Douwulai and chieftains including Pilouba and Lei led their followers to surrender.

On the wushen day Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain and greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin fled by night with several hundred horsemen of his retinue; his younger cousin Douwulai and his chieftain Piloubalie and others led their followers to surrender.
Chinese 匹婁拔累 is one personal name; splitting it into Pilouba and Lei invents a second person.

Day wushen: Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain, greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin with several hundred horsemen of his retinue fled by night; Shibin's younger cousin Douwulai and his chieftains Pilouba, Lei, and others led their followers to surrender.

Day wushen: Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain, greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin with several hundred horsemen of his retinue fled by night; Shibin's younger cousin Douwulai and his chieftain Piloubalie and others led their followers to surrender.
Chinese 匹婁拔累 is a single name, not two names Pilouba and Lei.
In the fourth month of summer the western Tiele rebelled; an edict ordered Tiansi, Prince of Ruyin, and Luo Yun, palace attendant giving, to campaign against them.
In the fourth month of summer the western Tiele rebelled; an edict ordered Tiansi, Prince of Ruyin, and Luo Yun, Palace Attendant (給事中), to campaign against them.
給事中 is the office title 'Palace Attendant' / 'Gentleman Attendant at the Palace'; 'giving' is a gloss error from 給 and is not English for the office.
Summer, fourth month: the western Tiele rebelled; an edict that Prince of Ruyin Tiansi and Palace Attendant Giving Luo Yun were to campaign against them.
Summer, fourth month: the western Tiele rebelled; an edict that Prince of Ruyin Tiansi and Palace Attendant Luo Yun were to campaign against them.
Same office mistranslation: 給事中 should not be rendered 'Palace Attendant Giving'.
Literal English inserts an extraneous closing parenthesis before the page-marker bracket; Chinese is (四七一)〉 with no such extra mark.
